sentences.en: Programming Throwdown, episode 50.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《编程大乱斗》第五十期。

sentences.en: Congratulations!
sentences.zh: 恭喜！

sentences.en: Take it away, Jason.
sentences.zh: 杰森，交给你了。

sentences.en: Hey, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: This is a special episode of Programming Throwdown.
sentences.zh: 这是一期特殊的《编程大乱斗》节目。

sentences.en: And, you know, if this is your first time listening to a Programming Throwdown episode, we typically talk about a different language or computational concept every show.
sentences.zh: 大家知道，如果这是你第一次收听《编程大乱斗》，我们通常每期节目都会讨论一种不同的语言或计算概念。

sentences.en: We start off with some news, tell some jokes, things like that.
sentences.zh: 我们从一些新闻开始，讲几个笑话，诸如此类。

sentences.en: We're not doing any of that this show.
sentences.zh: 我们这期节目不搞这些。

sentences.en: So if this is your first show that you've listened to, if you're brand new to Programming Throwdown, hit pause, go back a few episodes, check out one of our other ones.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这是你听的第一期节目，如果你是《编程大乱斗》的新听众，请按下暂停，返回前面几期，去听听我们的其他节目。

sentences.en: This is really just a special episode that we want to do for our fans, give them an opportunity to ask questions, make comments, and we'll read them on the air.
sentences.zh: 这其实只是一期我们想为粉丝们做的特别节目，让他们有机会提问、发表评论，我们会在节目中读出来。

sentences.en: And so we're also broadcasting this particular episode live on livecoding.tv slash neural nets for life, the number four.
sentences.zh: 所以我们也正在 livecoding.tv 斜杠 neural nets for life（数字 4）上对这期节目进行直播。

sentences.en: And we'll give a link to it in the show notes and all of that.
sentences.zh: 我们会在节目简介里提供链接之类的内容。

sentences.en: But that means that we're going to be fielding some questions from the live audience.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着我们要现场回答一些来自观众的问题。

sentences.en: And so that might cause us to, for one, it's definitely all one take.
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致，首先，这绝对是一气呵成录完的。

sentences.en: It usually is anyways.
sentences.zh: 通常也都是这样。

sentences.en: We always record this.
sentences.zh: 我们一直都是这样录音的。

sentences.en: People don't know that maybe, actually.
sentences.zh: 也许人们其实并不知道这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, good point.
sentences.zh: 对，说得好。

sentences.en: We always record in one take unless something really, really bad happens, which has only happened like once or twice where we've had probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我们总是录音一遍过，除非发生真的非常非常糟糕的事情——这种情况只发生过一两次，出了些问题。

sentences.en: But otherwise, it's one take all the way straight through, almost no editing, slap on the beginning and the end, which hopefully the beginning part has gotten a little better.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，都是从头到尾一气呵成，几乎不剪辑，只在片头和片尾加一下，希望开头部分现在已经做得好一点了。

sentences.en: I think people used to not like it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得以前大家可能不太喜欢。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, definitely have tightened that up.
sentences.zh: 对，对，这方面确实已经精简很多了。

sentences.en: Early, yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 早期的时候，对，完全是这样。

sentences.en: So in this episode, we're going to kind of talk about the history of the show and everything, give you guys an insight.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一期里，我们打算聊聊节目的历史之类的，让大家有个深入了解。

sentences.en: I've heard to say folks instead of guys.
sentences.zh: 我听到有人说“各位（folks）”而不是“伙计们（guys）”。

sentences.en: Folks.
sentences.zh: 各位。

sentences.en: Someone said don't say guys.
sentences.zh: 有人说别说“伙计们”。

sentences.en: Is that more politically correct?
sentences.zh: 这样更政治正确吗？

sentences.en: Say folks or yous, which I just can't do yous.
sentences.zh: 说“各位”或者“你们（yous）”，但我实在说不出口“yous”。

sentences.en: Y'all?
sentences.zh: “大家（y'all）”？

sentences.en: They also said y'all.
sentences.zh: 他们也提到了“y'all”。

sentences.en: I don't think I can do y'all either.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我也说不来“y'all”。

sentences.en: So I think I'm...
sentences.zh: 所以我想我还是……

sentences.en: All right, y'all.
sentences.zh: 好吧，各位。

sentences.en: Let's get this started.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: I'm relegating myself to folks.
sentences.zh: 我还是退而求其次用“各位”吧。

sentences.en: But give you folks an opportunity to ask us anything you want to ask us.
sentences.zh: 但我们要给各位一个机会，来问我们任何你们想问的问题。

sentences.en: And we've gotten a ton of questions and comments.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了海量的问题和评论。

sentences.en: And we're just going to kind of go through it and also field some from the chat as we go.
sentences.zh: 我们接下来会过一遍，同时也会随时挑选聊天室里的问题来回答。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The first one is one we've gotten several times.
sentences.zh: 第一个问题是我们收到了好几次的。

sentences.en: And we're going to only give a partial answer to, so apologies.
sentences.zh: 我们只打算给出一个部分的回答，所以在此道歉。

sentences.en: And sometimes there's been multiple questions and I sort of randomly picked a person to represent that question.
sentences.zh: 有时会有好几个类似的问题，我差不多是随机挑了一个人来代表那个问题。

sentences.en: And we didn't cover all questions.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有涵盖所有问题。

sentences.en: There are many, many questions about, will you cover topic X or Y?
sentences.zh: 有非常非常多关于“你们会讲 X 或 Y 主题吗？”的问题。

sentences.en: So those are left out.
sentences.zh: 所以那些就先略过了。

sentences.en: Don't feel bad if you email us with those.
sentences.zh: 如果你们发邮件问了这些，不要觉得不好意思。

sentences.en: Hopefully we'll cover all those eventually.
sentences.zh: 希望我们最终能把这些都讲到。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We've gotten so many people saying, will you cover Ruby?
sentences.zh: 我们收到好多人问：你们会讲 Ruby 吗？

sentences.en: We will cover Ruby, but not today.
sentences.zh: 我们会讲 Ruby，但不是今天。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So our first question is from Mariano.
sentences.zh: 我们的第一个问题来自马里亚诺（Mariano）。

sentences.en: And they say, I have a question.
sentences.zh: 他说，我有一个问题。

sentences.en: I have friends that are taking courses in edX.org, codeacademy.com, lynda.com, which are very useful websites to learn as a beginner going towards advanced.
sentences.zh: 我有些朋友在 edX.org、codeacademy.com、lynda.com 上学习课程，这些都是对初学者到进阶者非常实用的学习网站。

sentences.en: Being that the job market for programmers are majorly looking for a BA or MA, a bachelor or master's degree in computer science, would it be tough to get hired by learning to code
sentences.zh: 既然程序员的就业市场主要看重计算机科学的学士（BA、BS）或硕士学位，那么靠自学编程

sentences.en: on your own?
sentences.zh: 去找工作会很难吗？

sentences.en: Or what would be your experience?
sentences.zh: 或者根据你们的经验来看是怎样的？

sentences.en: And that's Mariano.
sentences.zh: 这是马里亚诺提的。

sentences.en: Cool, Mariano.
sentences.zh: 酷，马里亚诺。

sentences.en: You're the first question of the show.
sentences.zh: 你是本期节目的第一个问题。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜。

sentences.en: Woo, fanfare.
sentences.zh: 呜，号角响起。

sentences.en: So basically, this is a great question.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I actually thought a lot about this.
sentences.zh: 我其实对此思考了很多。

sentences.en: I asked a variety of people, personal friends and colleagues.
sentences.zh: 我问了各种各样的人，包括私下里的朋友和同事。

sentences.en: There's sort of an inflection point here.
sentences.zh: 这里其实存在一个转折点。

sentences.en: I mean, think about it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你想想看。

sentences.en: Five, 10 years ago, there was really only lynda.com.
sentences.zh: 五、十年前，真的只有 lynda.com。

sentences.en: There wasn't Coursera or- When this podcast started, we didn't have smartphones.
sentences.zh: 那时候没有 Coursera，或者说——在这个播客刚开始的时候，我们还没有智能手机。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or we had just gotten them.
sentences.zh: 或者说我们才刚拿到手。

sentences.en: I think you had just gotten one.
sentences.zh: 我想你当时刚拿到一部。

sentences.en: I didn't have one.
sentences.zh: 我当时没有。

sentences.en: I think what the iPhone, like 3GS was out.
sentences.zh: 我想当时 iPhone，比如 3GS 已经出来了。

sentences.en: Yeah, something like that.
sentences.zh: 对，差不多那样。

sentences.en: But yeah, basically, you know, since then, a lot has changed.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，基本上，你知道，从那以后，很多事情都变了。

sentences.en: It's changing very rapidly.
sentences.zh: 变化非常快。

sentences.en: And a lot of people are saying, look, Coursera has these amazing courses.
sentences.zh: 很多人说，你看，Coursera 有这些超棒的课程。

sentences.en: They're taught by MIT professors.
sentences.zh: 它们是由麻省理工学院的教授讲授的。

sentences.en: But, you know, when I apply for a job, you know, or if I'm hiring somebody, you know, how can I kind of take it seriously?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当我申请工作时，或者如果我在招聘别人时，你知道，我怎么能把它当回事呢？

sentences.en: You know, what's the accreditation level and things like that?
sentences.zh: 你知道，它的学历认证级别是怎样的，诸如此类？

sentences.en: It's a very difficult question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常难回答的问题。

sentences.en: This is the way I break it down.
sentences.zh: 我是这样来分析的。

sentences.en: If you have, you know, a bachelor's or a master's degree, that's always, you know, the gold standard, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你拥有学士或硕士学位，那一直都是，你知道的，黄金标准，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you get-
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你拿到——

sentences.en: They're accredited universities, and, you know, that's always going to be, you know, the best thing, right?
sentences.zh: 它们是获得认证的大学，你知道，那永远都会是，你知道最好的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: If you don't have that, it's good to have, you know, good background with Coursera, Udacity, these courses, combined with an active history on something like GitHub, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你没有那个，最好能拥有来自 Coursera、Udacity 这些课程的良好背景，再加上在像 GitHub 这样平台上的活跃历史，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you have a GitHub with a bunch of repositories, you've contributed a lot, you know, you are one of the authors of Homebrew or something like that,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一个包含一堆代码库的 GitHub 账号，你做出了很多贡献，你知道，你是 Homebrew 或类似项目的作者之一，

sentences.en: and you have some Coursera courses just to show that you picked up the fundamentals, then I think even if you, you know, don't have the college degree,
sentences.zh: 并且你有一些 Coursera 课程来证明你掌握了基础知识，那么我认为即使你没有大学学位，

sentences.en: I think you'll still get noticed.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你依然会被注意到。

sentences.en: And that's really the key.
sentences.zh: 而这才是真正的关键。

sentences.en: You know, once you're in an interview setting, your resume isn't as important.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一旦你进入了面试环节，你的简历就没那么重要了。

sentences.en: Most people will, you know, jump straight into- most people already know what three questions- like, they're going to ask you, hopefully not the FizzBuzz question and the,
sentences.zh: 大多数人会，你知道的，直接跳到——大多数人已经知道他们要问哪三个问题——比如，他们会问你，希望不是 FizzBuzz 问题，以及，

sentences.en: you know, some dynamic programming question.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，某些动态规划问题。

sentences.en: They know already what they're going to ask you, and if they see that you have a bachelor's in psychology, they're not going to redo the whole interview.
sentences.zh: 他们已经知道自己要问什么了，如果他们看到你拿的是心理学学士学位，他们也不会重新安排整场面试。

sentences.en: But the key is, how do you get to the interview stage with, and I have nothing against psychology, but how do you get to the interview stage with, you know,
sentences.zh: 但关键是，你该如何进入面试阶段——我并不是对心理学有意见，但你该如何凭借一个

sentences.en: a bachelor's that's not CS or engineering?
sentences.zh: 非计算机科学或工程学士学位进入面试阶段呢？

sentences.en: And so I think, again, you know, GitHub link should be the first thing on your resume, bunch of repositories, bunch of open source contributions, and the Coursera courses,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，再次强调，GitHub 链接应该是你简历上的第一项，一堆代码库，一堆开源贡献，还有 Coursera 课程，

sentences.en: and I think that can get your foot in the door.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这能让你敲开大门。

sentences.en: Yeah, I would agree.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意。

sentences.en: I think it'll be very difficult for having a boot camp or Udacity, even with their certificates and stuff, which they're getting better.
sentences.zh: 我觉得参加训练营或 Udacity 会非常困难，哪怕有他们的证书之类的东西，尽管它们现在越来越好了。

sentences.en: And in five years, this show may just seem completely dated.
sentences.zh: 而且在五年后，这档节目听起来可能完全过时了。

sentences.en: You pointed that out, that, like, this completely changes.
sentences.zh: 你刚才也指出了这一点，就是这些变化太快了。

sentences.en: But having worked for, with, and talking to people who also work at large companies, at least, there's a lot of filters because you get a lot of junk resumes in.
sentences.zh: 但为大公司工作过、与大公司合作过以及与大公司的人交谈过后，至少会发现里面有很多筛选门槛，因为你会收到大量垃圾简历。

sentences.en: And it's, as you said, how do you get into the, let's talk to these people, because once they talk to you, they may find out you're a great person to hire you, whatever.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如你所说，你怎么能进入“让我们和这些人聊聊”的环节呢？因为一旦他们和你谈过，他们可能会发现你是一个很棒的录用人选，不管怎样。

sentences.en: But how do you get into that pile?
sentences.zh: 但你如何进入那个候选堆里？

sentences.en: How do you get past that filter?
sentences.zh: 你如何通过那个筛选机制？

sentences.en: And as you said, it's, it's gonna be really hard.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这真的很难。

sentences.en: So I think somewhat you actually have, I don't know, I've never done this, but I would assume it may be something you have to take a chance on, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得某种程度上你确实得，我不知道，我从来没这么做过，但我猜这可能是一件你必须去冒险一试的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Like you have to take a job that isn't the job you would necessarily want.
sentences.zh: 比如你必须接受一份不一定是你真正想要的工作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: For pay, you might not necessarily want.
sentences.zh: 薪水可能也不是你想要的。

sentences.en: The GitHub stuff is, is great and that is necessary, but ultimately somebody is going to have to take the first risk on you.
sentences.zh: GitHub 上的东西很棒，而且也是必需的，但最终总得有人对你冒第一次险。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The thing about the Bachelor of Science or Master's or BA or whatever,
sentences.zh: 关于理学学士、硕士、文学学士或其他什么学位，

sentences.en: just Bachelor's degree or Master's degree or PhD is that you at least had the tenacities to stick through university,
sentences.zh: 只要是学士学位、硕士学位或博士学位，至少说明你有毅力坚持读完大学，

sentences.en: which is notoriously grueling, you know, to various degrees depending on the university.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，大学是非常折磨人的，根据大学的不同，折磨程度也有所不同。

sentences.en: And so the company is taking a bet that that is correlated with your ability to stick it and at least learn something and be productive at the company.
sentences.zh: 所以公司在押注，这与你坚持到底、至少学到一些东西并在公司发挥生产力的能力呈正相关。

sentences.en: And if you miss that, it's much harder.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有这个经历，就会难得多。

sentences.en: Not impossible, but it is much, much harder.
sentences.zh: 并非不可能，但确实难上加难。

sentences.en: And so you're going to have to do something to get your foot in the door.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须做点什么来敲开这扇门。

sentences.en: And that may mean taking a job that is, you know, you just volunteer, like for instance, to code for maybe a volunteer organization or a startup, you know,
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着去接受一份工作，你知道的，你只是去当志愿者，比如，为某个志愿组织或初创公司写代码，你知道的，

sentences.en: that's local to your area where, you know, hang out with them and like try to get involved there.
sentences.zh: 就在你当地的，你知道的，和他们混在一起，试着参与进去。

sentences.en: And even if they don't pay you, but at least you can start to, and not just say like, oh, hey, I work for these people when you didn't,
sentences.zh: 即使他们不付你薪水，但至少你可以开始——不是那种明明没做却说“哦，嘿，我为这些人工作过”的假话，

sentences.en: but get them to actually acknowledge your contribution so that you can honestly say like, hey, I work for this company.
sentences.zh: 而是让他们真正承认你的贡献，这样你就可以诚实地说：“嘿，我为这家公司工作过。”

sentences.en: Yep, yep.
sentences.zh: 对的，对的。

sentences.en: I know a lot of people at Mozilla are people who contributed massively to Firefox.
sentences.zh: 我知道 Mozilla 的很多人都是对 Firefox 做出过巨大贡献的人。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of, it's obvious when you think about it, but it's true.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仔细想想这挺显而易见的，但事实确实如此。

sentences.en: And now, you know, a lot of them also have degrees and things like that.
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道，他们当中很多人也有学位之类的。

sentences.en: But I think that showing a lot of contribution to some, you know, one thing a lot of people don't know, and we've talked about it several times, but it's been a while now,
sentences.zh: 但我认为展现出对某个东西的大量贡献——很多人不知道的一点，我们以前也说过好几次，不过已经隔了一段时间了——

sentences.en: is a lot of these open source projects are really run by large companies.
sentences.zh: 其实很多开源项目真的是由大公司运营的。

sentences.en: I mean, if you look at LibreOffice or Java is run, like IBM and Oracle are the two main contributors to Java, right, to the JVM.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你看看 LibreOffice，或者 Java 的运营，像 IBM 和 Oracle 是 Java（即 JVM）的两个主要贡献者，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, you know, contributing to those open source projects directly connects you with a lot of engineers in the industry.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，直接为这些开源项目做贡献，能让你与业内许多工程师建立联系。

sentences.en: So that's something to keep in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以这是需要记住的一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, and those engineers can put in your resume, and an engineer putting in your resume having noticed you is always going to be better than...
sentences.zh: 是的，那些工程师可以在你的简历上帮你内推，而且注意到你的工程师帮你内推，效果总是比……

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: ...applying blindly.
sentences.zh: ……盲目投递要好。

sentences.en: So that's another tip, is like, if you know someone, always have them put in your resume, because that universally leads to better results, in my experience.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是一个秘诀，就是如果你认识某个人，一定要让他们帮你内推，根据我的经验，这普遍能带来更好的结果。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we should also preface, someone pointed out in the chat room, that most of our advice is oriented to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们还得先说明一下，聊天室里有人指出，我们的大多数建议都是针对美国的。

sentences.en: Some of it may be applicable elsewhere, but, you know, Jason and I both live in the U.S., and I have lived in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 其中有些可能适用于其他地方，但是，你知道，杰森和我都在美国生活，我这辈子也一直

sentences.en: all my life, and so I don't know.

sentences.en: Bug fixes.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's really easy early on to just be like, oh, I got down to the last little bit of something and, uh, that's good enough.
sentences.zh: 在早期很容易就会觉得，哦，我把最后一点小东西搞定了，嗯，这就够了。

sentences.en: Like I got to this hard part.
sentences.zh: 就像我遇到了这个难点。

sentences.en: I'll just like, eh, I'll just go ahead and move on.
sentences.zh: 我就会，呃，干脆继续前进了。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's like, no, no, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 然后就会觉得，不，不，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: Like often that's where like the good learning happens because you are really terrible at identifying the easy and hard parts in the beginning.
sentences.zh: 通常好玩的地方或好的学习正是在那里发生的，因为你在开始时实在太不擅长识别哪些是简单部分，哪些是困难部分了。

sentences.zh: 至少我是这样的。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Same here.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: I often misidentify them.
sentences.zh: 我经常搞错它们。

sentences.en: Uh, the other thing is refactor your code and a corollary of that is write your code expecting to refactor it.
sentences.zh: 呃，另一件事是重构你的代码，由此引申出来的一个推论是，写代码时就要预期到以后会重构它。

sentences.en: And so what that means is don't try and solve all the world's problems or the next five years worth of problems at your company right now, because it changes frequently.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着现在不要试图解决世界上所有的问题，或者你公司未来五年的问题，因为情况经常在变。

sentences.en: You're not really going to get it right anyways, and you're going to waste a lot of time.
sentences.zh: 反正你也不太可能完全弄对，而且你会浪费很多时间。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: The flip side of that is...
sentences.zh: 硬币的另一面是……

sentences.en: A delicate balance, yeah.
sentences.zh: 微妙的平衡，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you're going to code based on this year's problems, then make sure everybody knows that next year you're going to rewrite a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 如果你要根据今年的问题来写代码，那么请确保每个人都知道明年你要重写很大一部分。

sentences.en: I think you have to strike some balance there.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须在那里找到某种平衡。

sentences.en: Like, and the thing I've been trying to do is strike the balance of things which I have more confidence that won't change, I'll spend more time on.
sentences.zh: 比如，我一直在尝试做的事情是，对于那些我更有信心不会改变的东西，我会花更多时间。

sentences.en: And things which I think are likely to change, less time on.
sentences.zh: 而对于那些我认为很可能会改变的东西，我会少花时间。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, um, like I'll do them a little more hacky, a little more, you know, rough around the edges and let that be okay until we are sure we want to do that.
sentences.zh: 但是，呃，我会把它们写得有点凑合，稍微，你知道的，粗糙一点，在确保我们真正想那么做之前，先让它这样也没关系。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, and that's a objective, subjective decision, so.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个客观兼主观的决定，所以。

sentences.en: And you should be proud to redo your code.
sentences.zh: 而且你应该为重做代码感到自豪。

sentences.en: I mean, like definitely don't get, uh, I've seen this where some people get sort of defensive about their code.
sentences.zh: 我是说，绝对不要，呃，我见过这种情况，有些人对自己的代码有防御心理。

sentences.en: I mean, they look at it as sort of their territory, like, oh, you're wiping my name off the map, you know?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们把代码看作是自己的领地，比如，哦，你在把我的名字从地图上抹去，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it's like, uh, I feel like, you know, if your name isn't wiped off the map in five years, then, then there's some old code that probably needs to be rewritten.
